## Problem 1 - OOP Programming

### (a) For the waldCI class, define the following:

```{r}
# define the waldCI class
setClass("waldCI",
          slots = c(level = "numeric",
                    mean = "numeric",
                    sterr = "numeric"))

# check waldCI objects have valid calues
setValidity("waldCI", function(object){
  if(object@level <= 0 | object@level >= 1) {
    stop("level must be in (0, 1)")
  }
  if(object@sterr <= 0) {
    stop("stderr must be positive")
  }
  if(!is.finite(object@sterr)) {
    stop("Infinite CI not supported")
  }
  return(TRUE)
})
```
```{r}
makeCI <- function(level,
                   lb = NULL,
                   ub = NULL,
                   mean = NULL,
                   sterr = NULL) {
  
  # create the object directly for mean and standard error
  if (!is.null(mean) && !is.null(stderr) &&
        is.null(lb) && is.null(ub)) {
    return(new("waldCI", level = level, mean = mean, sterr = sterr))
    
  } else if (is.null(mean) && is.null(sterr) &&
               !is.null(lb) && !is.null(ub)) {
    
    # check that the lower bound is smaller than the upper
    if (lb > ub) {
      stop("lb must be less than ub")
    }
    
    # calculate the mean and standard error from the interval bounds
    z <- qnorm((1 + level) / 2)
    mean <- (lb + ub) / 2
    sterr   <- (ub - lb) / (2 * z)
    return(new("waldCI", level = level, mean = mean, sterr = sterr))
  } else {
    
    # require either lb/ub or mean/sterr
    stop("Input must be either lb/ub or mean/sterr")
  }
}
```

'show' method
```{r}
# calculate the lower and upper CI bounds
.getBounds <- function(ci) {
  z <- qnorm((1 + ci@level)/2)
  lb <- ci@mean - z*ci@sterr
  ub <- ci@mean + z*ci@sterr
  return(c(lb, ub))
}

# show method for waldCI object
setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {
  bound <- .getBounds(object)
  cat(round(object@level*100))
  cat("% CI: (")
  cat(bound[1])
  cat(", ")
  cat(bound[2])
  cat(")\n")
  return(invisible(object))
})
```

Accessors:

```{r}
# get values from the object
.getSlot <- function(object, slotname) {
  if (slotname %in% c("level", "mean", "sterr")) {
    return(slot(object, slotname))
  }
  
  # calculate bounds when lb or ub is requested
  bounds <- .getBounds(object)
  if (slotname == "lb") {
    return(bounds[1])
  } else if (slotname == "ub") {
    return(bounds[2])
  } else {
    stop("Invalid slotname")
  }
}

# define the level generic
setGeneric("level", function(object) {
  standardGeneric("level")
})
```
```{r}
# define the level method for waldCI objects
setMethod("level", "waldCI", function(object) .getSlot(object, "level"))

# define the mean method for waldCI objects

# define a generic function for sterr()
setGeneric("sterr", function(object) {

})
```

contains and overlaps
```{r}
# check whether a value is inside the CI
contains <- function(ci, value) {
  stopifnot(is.numeric(value))
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  bounds <- .getBounds(ci)
  return(value > bounds[1] & value < bounds[2])
}

# check whether two CI overlap
overlap <- function(ci1, ci2) {
  b1 <- .getBounds(ci1)
  b2 <- .getBounds(ci2)
  return(max(b1[1], b2[1]) <= min(b1[2], b2[2]))
}
```

as.numeric:
```{r}
# covert waldCI to numeric
setGeneric("as.numeric")
```

```{r}
setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x) {
  return(.getBounds(x))
})
```

transform:

```{r}
# apply a monotonic transformation to a `waldCI`
transformCI <- function(ci, fn) {
  stopifnot(is.function(fn))
  stopifnot(is(ci, "waldCI"))
  return(makeCI(level = ci@level,
                mean = fn(ci@mean),
                sterr = fn(ci@sterr)))
}
```

ci1

### (c) Show that your validator does not allow the creation of invalid confidence intervals:

```{r}
# negative standard error
makeCI(.9, mean = 3, sterr = -2)
```
```{r}
# lower bound greater than upper bound
makeCI(.9, lb = 5, ub = 2)
```

```{r}
# infinite bounds
makeCI(.9, lb = 2, ub = Inf)
```

```{r}
# invalid use of setters
mean(ci1) <- "a"
lb(ci1) <- 30
sterr(ci1) <- -2
sterr(ci1) <- Inf
```
## Problem 2 - data.table
```{r}
library(data.table)
tennis_dt <- as.data.table(copy(tennis))
```

### (a) How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
# combine all Davis Cup matches under one tournament name
tennis_dt[, tourney_name2 := fifelse(
  grepl("^Davis", tourney_name),
  "Davis Cup",
  tourney_name
)]

# count unique tournaments
tournaments <- unique(tennis_dt[, .(tourney_name2)])

nrow(tournaments)
```
There were 69 unique tournaments in 2019.

### (b) Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?
```{r}
# count tournament wins for each player
winners <- tennis_dt[
  round == "F",
  .(wins = .N),
  by = winner_name
][
  wins > 1
][
  order(-wins)
]

# number of players who won more than one tournament
nrow(winners)

# player(s) with the most tournament wins
winners[wins == max(wins)]
```
Yes. 12 players won more than one tournament. Novak Djokovic and Dominic Thiem had the most tournament wins, with 5 each.

### (c) Do winners have more aces than losers?
```{r}
# check whether the winner had more aces in each match
ace_stats <- tennis_dt[
  ,
  .(win_more = w_ace > l_ace)
][
  !is.na(win_more),
  .(
    x = sum(win_more),
    n = .N
  )
]

ace_stats
```
```{r}
prop.test(
  ace_stats$x,
  ace_stats$n,
  p = 0.5
)
```
There is statistically significant evidence that winners have more aces than losers in more than half of the matches.
